notes: The file is a Spanish translation, not the English original. Its cover page (opened) says: 'Please cite the original article: Fearnside, P.M. 1985. A stochastic model for estimating human carrying capacity in Brazil's Transamazon Highway colonization area. Human Ecology 13(3): 331-369. Doi: 10.1007/BF01558255', and the translation carries revision dates up to 15 March 1993. The original was not opened, so any figure attributed to it is read through a translation. The 2,500 and 2,550 kcal and 25 g animal protein values are present in the translation. 42 pages. B_OUT and MT say the method detail was read from this file.

title: Fearnside 1990 (the 1990 paper, 'a five-page overview')
what_taken: Concept of capacity as a density-by-failure curve; the one result: at most 0.24 persons a hectare for a 23,600 ha Trans-Amazon study area, against 0.5 to 1 in the FAO/UNFPA/IIASA study; the FAO calculation that Brazil could support over seven billion
notes: The file has no extension; file(1) says PDF, 5 pages. Page 1 (opened): 'Estimation of Human Carrying Capacity in Rainforest Areas', Philip M. Fearnside, TREE vol. 5, no. 6, June 1990 (pages 192 onward; PII S0169-5347(90)90209-V). The 0.24 persons per hectare for 23,600 ha and the 0.5 to 1 figure are confirmed in the text (lines 364 and 847 to 851).
